name: Archives and records management
one_line: The one government situation whose evidence is a representation of custody over records the holder did not author: accession and transfer instruments, multilevel archival description, retention and disposal scheduling, preservation and fixity records, and access or closure review. It is not activated by the word archive, by an archives institution's name, by a .zip container, by a folder named Archive, by age, or by retention vocabulary. Its distinct default against the government schema is (a) a description/described-item seam that no other government row has - the file in hand is metadata about files not in hand - and (b) a privacy rule that runs inside a single packet rather than across it, because a finding aid may be publishable while the item it describes is closed and the donor and closure files are more sensitive than either. Placeholder launch (J-IND): it writes NO field rows, because the government schema declares none under PR-6 and D1's deferral stands.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every signal below is template-activation evidence only. The government schema declares no field rows, so no accepted signal licenses an archival fact. In particular a description must never write its described item's facts, and an item must never inherit its description's.

a multilevel archival description in one document or XML file: nested description levels (collection or fonds, series, sub-series, file, item) where each level carries its own scope-and-content, covering dates, extent, and conditions-of-access slots, and where the reference code of a child is a prefix-extension of its parent's

an accession, transfer or deposit instrument naming a depositing body or donor on one side and a receiving repository as custodian on the other, with extent, date of transfer, statement of title or custody, and a conditions-of-access or restriction clause; the decisive structure is the custody handover, not the subject matter of what is handed over

an accession register, transfer box list, or location register whose ROWS ARE OTHER RECORDS - series or box title, covering date range, extent, provenance note, appraisal decision, closure flag, shelf or store location - rather than rows recording actions the holding body itself took

a retention and disposal schedule whose rows pair a named record series with a trigger event, a retention period, and a final action of transfer, review, or destruction, held together with, or cross-referenced by, a disposal or destruction certificate naming an authorising officer, method, and the series destroyed

a preservation package layout read from an archive manifest without unpacking: a bag-style directory with a bag-info descriptor and a checksum manifest over a payload directory, or a submission/archival/dissemination package naming convention, where the payload members are themselves heterogeneous records

preservation-event rows in a log or CSV shaped as event type, date, agent, outcome, and object identifier, where event types are custody operations such as fixity check, virus scan, format migration, normalisation, or repackaging

a format-identification or characterisation report keyed by persistent format identifiers with per-format counts and an explicitly reported unidentified residue, run over an accession rather than over the holder's working files

an access or closure review record that pairs an exact archival reference code with an opening or closed-until date and a reasoning slot, and that is a separate document from the item whose access it governs
a reading-room production, retrieval, or reprographics request naming a reader and a list of reference codes to be produced from a store
needs_llm: deciding whether a document is an archival DESCRIPTION OF a corpus or a MEMBER OF it, when both legitimately carry the same reference code - the hardest call this row makes, and the one that must abstain rather than guess

separating a repository's own corporate records (its board minutes, its staff rota, its budget) from the holdings it has custody of; the repository is a public body like any other and its own paperwork belongs to the ordinary authority-side rows
reading an unlabelled prose letter or email for custody-transfer intent when no form slots exist, e.g. a departmental message offering old case files to a records centre

deciding whether a records-management policy, file plan, or retention schedule belongs to a public authority's own recordkeeping function or to a private company, when the issuing body is not independently evidenced as public
deciding whether a digitisation master is being kept as a preservation object under custody or simply as a scan someone made
judging whether an appraisal note is a custody decision about a series or an ordinary internal opinion about a document
never_alone: the words Archive, Archives, Fonds, Collection, Catalogue, Repository, Record Office, Records Centre, or Recordkeeping alone, and a named archives institution alone; the institution may be a research venue, a citation source, an employer, a donor, a download origin, or a place someone visited

source_type archive, or a .zip / .tar / .7z extension, or a filename containing Archive - a compressed container is not archival custody, and the design says to “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”. This is the trap that Site Photos Archive.zip sets.
a parent folder named Archive, Archives, Old, Backup, Legacy, or Historic, and equally a user-chosen “dedicated archive location” used as a filesystem root; a storage tier is not a custodial function
an archival-looking reference code alone, or a bare accession-shaped number; a bare number carries no domain, and hierarchical codes also occur as invoice, drawing, part, and case numbers

retention vocabulary alone - a retention period, a disposal action word, a legal citation, a destroy-by date, or a legal-hold notice; the same vocabulary appears in corporate policy, cloud storage lifecycle settings, mailbox rules, and litigation holds
age alone - an old covering date, a scanned handwritten page, historic letterhead, or a document about the past; a repository holds recent records and a family holds Victorian ones
a checksum or fixity manifest alone; backup tools, package managers, download verifiers, and disk imagers all emit one, and a manifest with no custody context proves only that bytes were hashed

a person's or family's own carefully arranged papers, letters, photographs, or scans; private custody of one's own material is Photos or Personal, not an authority-side repository, however archival the arrangement looks
a public body's name, seal, letterhead, .gov-style domain, or PDF producer string alone; that is the government schema's own never-alone rule and it applies unchanged here
a shared download session or browser batch that pulled many catalogue PDFs at once; “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
missing EXIF or dense OCR as proof that an image of a catalogue record is a screenshot; “the system must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot”

work_types: arrangement and description: finding aid, catalogue entry, box list, or authority record
retention and disposal schedule or file plan
preservation action record: fixity check, migration, normalisation, repackaging
digitisation batch record and preservation-master register
access and closure review, opening record, or redaction record on the custody side
reader registration, production request, and reprographics order
records survey, location register, and store or environmental monitoring record
records-management policy, procedure, or custody agreement
grouping_reasons: one accession or transfer lifecycle, linked by an exact accession or transfer reference across the transfer instrument, box list, appraisal note, format report, and preservation log

one collection or fonds, linked by a hierarchical reference-code prefix shared across description levels; the prefix relationship is structural evidence, not a licence to copy a collection label onto a member

one ingest or preservation package, linked by a bag or object identifier read from a manifest; “Archives should be inspected without being unpacked to disk” and this row never unpacks one merely to strengthen recognition
one disposal action, linking a schedule row, an authorisation, and a certificate; the destroyed series is described by these files and is not present in them

the DESCRIPTION and the DESCRIBED ITEM stay in different groups even when they share a reference code exactly; this is the row's defining grouping rule and the one a naive exact-match join would break
reader, donor, and closure files stay in a protected group of their own rather than joining the public description group they point at
duplicate and version families remain universal relationships; successive versions of a finding aid or a retention schedule acquire no new facts from their neighbourhood
no group is a valid outcome; a standalone catalogue printout or single transfer receipt with no lifecycle around it is “a durable purpose but no broader group” and belongs in Independent Records

template.why: Empty by contract, not by absence of structure: PR-6 leaves the government schema fieldless and a template cannot branch on undeclared fields. The recommendation this row would make if fields were ever ratified is recorded here as prose only. The custody unit - collection, fonds, or accession - would come first, because a series or item description is unintelligible without it, exactly as “A work type such as Homework 3 is meaningful only after the course is known.” Description level or custody function would follow, then work type. Covering dates would come last and never first, both because “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders” and because this world carries three unrelated dates at once - the covering dates of the described material, the accession date, and the preservation-event date - so a single time level would be actively misleading. Donor, depositor, and reader names must never become a dimension. Any such order would remain the user's to change: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: Both worlds sit on the records-holder side and both produce access decisions with exemption reasoning. The shared fixture is a document that names a reference and refuses or defers access. This row requires a custody workflow - the file governs an item already accessioned and described, and its horizon is an opening date. The FOI row requires a request workflow - an external requester, a request reference, a statutory clock, and a response. Disclosure Schedule for FOI Request 2026-118 is theirs; Access Review for MS-0603-14 closed until 2059 is this row's. A redaction record alone decides nothing.

The closest neighbour by far: accessioning, donor instruments, catalogue description, condition and preservation records, and loan or access control all occur identically on both sides. The same deed of gift shape appears in both. The discriminator is the unit of description and what it is a description of: this row describes records arising from an activity, arranged in a provenance hierarchy where a child reference extends its parent's and the described unit is a series or file; the museum row describes objects catalogued individually with material, dimension, condition and display slots. A collection-level record with neither hierarchy nor object slots is undecidable and abstains.

Cataloguing, format identification, digitisation batches, and reading-room operations look the same on both sides, and one institution frequently runs both. The discriminator is uniqueness and provenance: library description is of published items that exist in many copies, keyed to bibliographic identifiers and holdings counts; archival description is of unique material keyed to provenance and hierarchy. A digitisation batch record follows whichever description it is bound to; a bare reading-room production request follows the code system on the request.

The broad authority-side row and this row compete over every retention schedule, file plan, and records-management policy an authority writes about its OWN files, and over the repository's own corporate paperwork. The boundary is custody of other bodies' records: a schedule governing the authority's live files while they remain in its own business use is the broad row's; the same schedule cited by a transfer instrument or a disposal certificate that moves or destroys a series under a custodial function is this row's. The repository's own board minutes and budget always belong to the broad row.

Grandma letters and photos - sorted by year.zip competes directly with an accession packet: scanned historic material, a contents list, chronological arrangement, old covering dates. Photos owns it whenever the custody is the holder's own or their family's. This row requires an evidenced repository receiving material from a separate depositing body under an instrument. Age, arrangement quality, and the word archive are worthless on both sides of this edge.

A closed-file store, deeds packet, or matter-archive index has custody vocabulary, retention periods, destruction certificates and a box list, and is often literally called an archive. That row owns it whenever the custody is a practitioner holding client files under a representation. This row requires a public repository holding transferred records under a custodial function rather than a professional duty to a client. A destruction certificate alone does not decide the edge; the holder-role evidence does.

falls_through_to.when: a readable standalone catalogue printout, transfer receipt, retention schedule, format report, or preservation log has durable value but no accepted custody lifecycle around it
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: a donor or depositor file, closure review, reader or production record, or a described item containing named-person material lacks a safe accepted group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: an unlabelled transfer letter, an ambiguous retention document, or a description that cannot be separated from the item it describes leaves the custody question unresolved
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.when: an encrypted or damaged package, an unreadable catalogue-system export, or an unknown preservation binary yields nothing beyond metadata
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

falls_through_to.when: a published catalogue guide, archival standard, preservation article, or repository annual report is held for reading rather than as custody work
falls_through_to.design_cite: Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.

falls_through_to.when: a positively evidenced screen capture of a catalogue or repository system has no accepted custody group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.

sensitivity_why: The posture is unusual and cannot be set once for the packet. A finding aid may be intended for publication while the item it describes is closed for decades, and the donor agreement, appraisal note, closure justification, and reader production record are frequently more sensitive than either - they name donors, name living individuals described in closed material, and reveal who consulted what. The described holdings themselves may be citizen casework, personnel, health, adoption, care, policing, or security material. Because the design requires that “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector” and that “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it”, the safe default is potentially_sensitive for the whole row, with donor, closure, and reader material treated as the strictest members. A closure or restriction legend found in a document is retained as a literal observation only; it is not a handling class and P7 owns that vocabulary.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: (1) the description/described-item seam has no representation in the current model - P9 needs a way to record that file A describes corpus B without an exact-reference join copying facts between them, and this row cannot author it. (2) If PR-6 is lifted, decide centrally whether a custody-unit concept (collection or accession), a description level, and an archival reference code may exist as government fields and whether any is destination-eligible; this row deliberately proposes none. (3) Decide whether a retention or disposal period may ever influence the residual review lifecycle, given that the design already forbids deletion and disposability marking without explicit user action. (4) Decide how public-repository status is established for hybrid, university, diocesan, and corporate repositories that behave archivally but are not public bodies - gazetteer, user confirmation, or abstention.
